identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: The Maa Sharda Temple crowns Trikuta hill above the town of Maihar and is regarded by devotees as a Shakti Peetha, associated with the Goddess as an incarnation of Saraswati. Tradition credits its discovery to the legendary warrior-brothers Alha and Udal.

narrative.summaryIntro: The Maa Sharda Temple sits atop Trikuta hill overlooking the town of Maihar in Madhya Pradesh. Regarded by devotees as a Shakti Peetha and an incarnation of Saraswati, the shrine is traditionally linked to the warrior-brothers Alha and Udal, who are said to have discovered it and, according to legend, still visit before dawn.
narrative.documentedHistory: Temple tradition holds that the site is where Sati's necklace fell, following Vishnu's division of her body into 51 parts after her self-immolation, giving it status as a Shakti Peetha. A separate legend credits the legendary brothers Alha and Udal with discovering the shrine on Trikuta hill and, after twelve years of penance by Alha, receiving a boon of immortality from the Goddess; folk tradition holds Alha still visits the temple in the Brahma Muhurta before dawn.
